title: Grateful Dead Live at Eastown Theater on 1971-10-23
source: SBD -> Master Reel (7 Inch - 1/2 Track) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/96k) -> FLAC/24

ai_review.summary: Clear early‑70s soundboard capture of a classic Detroit show with standout Cumberland Blues and jammy Truckin, but mixed energy due to a restless audience
ai_review.review: The Miller‑sourced soundboard recording is generally crisp and captures the early ’71 tone that fans love, aside from a brief FM glitch in “Bertha”. Musically the concert delivers solid performances—blazing Cumberland Blues, a jammy Truckin, and an exciting NFA/GDTR sequence—but the night was marred by a vocal, demanding crowd and fewer segues than usual, giving it a mixed‑feel vibe.

ai_rating.rationale: Weighted average of show (≈4) and recording quality (≈4.5) yields ~4.2; many positive reviews with consistent praise for sound and performance, balanced by a few strong negative comments.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear early‑70s soundboard capture with crisp tone; occasional brief FM interference in "Bertha" noted but overall very listenable.

standout_songs: NFA/GDTR (Not Fade Away / The Other One segment)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Classic early‑71 setlist with solid playing, but the show suffered from long tuning breaks and a lack of segues, reflecting tension between band and audience.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his early ’70s guitar tone; occasional quirky lyric moment noted in "Tennessee Jed".
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s dry remarks were highlighted, suggesting a slightly disengaged vibe.
band_member_comments.Keys: Early Keith (first tour) playing appreciated; keyboards add the period flavor.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy Cobham‑style drumming praised; fans love the shows with just Billy on drums.
